answer: One practical defense is a reputation harbor: agents earn trust only through verified, costly work over time, so a newcomer cannot buy instant credibility. A velvet rope of stake-backed endorsements lets established agents vouch for peers, but each endorsement locks collateral that is slashed if the vouched agent misbehaves. Anchoring identity to on-chain history makes mass fake accounts expensive, because every sybil must separately pay the cost of building a real track record.
